### Common table expression

**Aliases:** CTE, `WITH` query, `MATERIALIZED`, `NOT MATERIALIZED`, `CommonTableExpr`. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

A common table expression is a named auxiliary query written in a `WITH` clause and referenced by the main query like a table ([queries.sgml#queries-with](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/queries.sgml#L2047-L2062)). The parser stores each one as a `CommonTableExpr` node, whose `ctematerialized` field records `MATERIALIZED`, `NOT MATERIALIZED` or no choice ([parsenodes.h#CTEMaterialize](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1636-L1641), [parsenodes.h#CommonTableExpr](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1668-L1680)). The choice matters to the planner. `SS_process_ctes()` inlines a non-recursive, side-effect-free `SELECT` CTE as a subquery when it is marked `NOT MATERIALIZED`, or when it has no marking and only one reference. A multiply-referenced CTE is still not inlined if it refers to an outer recursive CTE ([subselect.c#SS_process_ctes](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L934-L951)). A `SELECT` CTE that nothing references is dropped ([subselect.c:900-908](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L900-L908)). Otherwise the planner plans the CTE separately as a [SubPlan](#subplan) ([subselect.c#SS_process_ctes](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L991-L997)). A separately planned CTE is normally evaluated at most once per execution of the parent query, and the planner cannot push the parent's conditions down into a multiply-referenced one ([queries.sgml#queries-with-cte-materialization](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/queries.sgml#L2500-L2518)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds, with the same three markings, inlining rule and dropping of unreferenced `SELECT` CTEs ([parsenodes.h#CTEMaterialize](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1417-L1422), [subselect.c#SS_process_ctes](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L882-L899), [subselect.c:848-856](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L848-L856)). 12's `CommonTableExpr` has no `SEARCH` or `CYCLE` clause fields ([parsenodes.h#CommonTableExpr](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1424-L1441)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds ([parsenodes.h#CTEMaterialize](../raw/postgres-14/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1464-L1469), [subselect.c#SS_process_ctes](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L947-L964), [subselect.c:913-921](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L913-L921)). As in 17, `CommonTableExpr` has `search_clause` and `cycle_clause` fields ([parsenodes.h:1504-1505](../raw/postgres-14/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1504-L1505)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds ([parsenodes.h#CTEMaterialize](../raw/postgres-18/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1665-L1670), [subselect.c#SS_process_ctes](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L934-L951), [subselect.c:900-908](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L900-L908)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds ([parsenodes.h#CTEMaterialize](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1666-L1671), [subselect.c#SS_process_ctes](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L943-L960), [subselect.c:909-917](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L909-L917)).

Related: [Planner](#planner), [Parse tree](#parse-tree), [Function volatility](#function-volatility)

### CONCURRENTLY

**Aliases:** CIC (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`), RIC (`REINDEX CONCURRENTLY`), `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

For index commands, `CONCURRENTLY` builds, rebuilds or drops an index without blocking writes to the table. A concurrent build or rebuild does more total work: it scans the table twice and waits for older transactions to finish ([ref/create_index.sgml#sql-createindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L612-L625), [ref/reindex.sgml#sql-reindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/reindex.sgml#L367-L380), [ref/drop_index.sgml:46-50](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/drop_index.sgml#L46-L50)). The same keyword is also an option of `ALTER TABLE ... DETACH PARTITION` and `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW`; this entry covers the index commands ([gram.y:2326-2327](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L2326-L2327), [gram.y:4812](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L4812)). In source, `DefineIndex()` takes a [ShareUpdateExclusiveLock](#shareupdateexclusivelock) instead of `ShareLock` when the option is set ([indexcmds.c:678](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c#L678)). `index_set_state_flags()` flips the [pg_index](#pg_index) state flags, and the build commits between steps: it enters the index as invalid in one transaction and runs the two table scans in two more ([index.c#index_set_state_flags](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L3469-L3503), [ref/create_index.sgml#sql-createindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L627-L643)). `ReindexRelationConcurrently()` implements `REINDEX CONCURRENTLY`. It first adds a new transient index definition to `pg_index` to replace the old index ([indexcmds.c#ReindexRelationConcurrently](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c#L3428-L3451), [ref/reindex.sgml#sql-reindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/reindex.sgml#L382-L394)). A failed concurrent build leaves an [invalid index](#invalid-index) behind ([ref/create_index.sgml#sql-createindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L646-L650)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds, except for two limits. `ALTER TABLE ... DETACH PARTITION` has no `CONCURRENTLY` option in 12, and `REINDEX CONCURRENTLY` on a partitioned table only warns and skips it ([gram.y:2033-2034](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L2033-L2034), [indexcmds.c:2917-2922](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c#L2917-L2922)). 12 is the first release with `REINDEX CONCURRENTLY` ([release-12.sgml:4631-4633](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/release-12.sgml#L4631-L4633)). The docs describe the two table scans and the waits, `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY` and `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` exist, `DefineIndex()` takes `ShareUpdateExclusiveLock` instead of `ShareLock`, and `index_set_state_flags()` and `ReindexRelationConcurrently()` exist ([ref/create_index.sgml#sql-createindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L544-L556), [ref/reindex.sgml#sql-reindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/ref/reindex.sgml#L284-L313), [ref/drop_index.sgml:46-50](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/ref/drop_index.sgml#L46-L50), [gram.y:4113](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L4113), [indexcmds.c:563](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c#L563), [index.c:3332](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L3332), [indexcmds.c#ReindexRelationConcurrently](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c#L2715-L2739)). A failed build leaves an invalid index ([ref/create_index.sgml#sql-createindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L574-L580)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds. `DETACH PARTITION` and `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` accept `CONCURRENTLY`, `DefineIndex()` takes `ShareUpdateExclusiveLock` instead of `ShareLock`, `index_set_state_flags()` walks the `pg_index` states, and `ReindexRelationConcurrently()` adds a transient index ([gram.y:2130-2131](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L2130-L2131), [gram.y:4317](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L4317), [indexcmds.c:663](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c#L663), [index.c#index_set_state_flags](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L3467-L3539), [indexcmds.c:3384](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c#L3384), [ref/reindex.sgml#sql-reindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-14/doc/src/sgml/ref/reindex.sgml#L352-L374)). `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY` drops without locking out writes, and a failed build leaves an invalid index ([ref/drop_index.sgml:46-50](../raw/postgres-14/doc/src/sgml/ref/drop_index.sgml#L46-L50), [ref/create_index.sgml#sql-createindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-14/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L632-L636)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds. The docs, the two grammar uses, the `ShareUpdateExclusiveLock` choice in `DefineIndex()`, `index_set_state_flags()`, and `ReindexRelationConcurrently()` are unchanged ([ref/create_index.sgml#sql-createindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-18/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L618-L649), [ref/drop_index.sgml:46-50](../raw/postgres-18/doc/src/sgml/ref/drop_index.sgml#L46-L50), [gram.y:2339-2340](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L2339-L2340), [gram.y:4926](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L4926), [indexcmds.c:681](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c#L681), [index.c#index_set_state_flags](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L3523-L3557), [indexcmds.c#ReindexRelationConcurrently](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c#L3561-L3584)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds. The docs still describe two table scans and waits, `DETACH PARTITION` and `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` still accept the keyword, `DefineIndex()` still picks `ShareUpdateExclusiveLock` over `ShareLock`, `index_set_state_flags()` still steps the `pg_index` flags, and `ReindexRelationConcurrently()` still adds a transient index first ([ref/create_index.sgml#sql-createindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L618-L646), [ref/drop_index.sgml:46-50](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/ref/drop_index.sgml#L46-L50), [gram.y:2410-2411](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L2410-L2411), [gram.y:5006](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L5006), [indexcmds.c:685](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c#L685), [index.c#index_set_state_flags](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L3615-L3625), [indexcmds.c#ReindexRelationConcurrently](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/commands/indexcmds.c#L3590-L3612), [ref/reindex.sgml#sql-reindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/ref/reindex.sgml#L385-L396)). A failed build still leaves an invalid index ([ref/create_index.sgml#sql-createindex-concurrently](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L650-L673)). 19 also offers `REPACK (CONCURRENTLY)`, a table rewrite rather than an index command ([mvcc.sgml:1101-1103](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/mvcc.sgml#L1101-L1103)).

### Conflict detection

**Aliases:** logical replication conflict, `ConflictType`, `insert_exists`, `update_origin_differs`, `ReportApplyConflict`. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

In PostgreSQL 18, conflict detection is the subscriber-side code that classifies, logs and counts cases where an incoming [logical replication](#logical-replication) change does not fit the local data. It lives in `conflict.c` ([conflict.c:1-12](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/replication/logical/conflict.c#L1-L12)). `ConflictType` names seven cases, such as `CT_INSERT_EXISTS` for a unique-key clash and `CT_UPDATE_ORIGIN_DIFFERS` for a row last changed by a different origin ([conflict.h#ConflictType](../raw/postgres-18/src/include/replication/conflict.h#L31-L59)). `ReportApplyConflict()` counts each conflict in `pg_stat_subscription_stats` and then reports it at the level its caller passes: `ERROR` for a unique-key clash, `LOG` for the other cases ([conflict.c#ReportApplyConflict](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/replication/logical/conflict.c#L103-L131), [execReplication.c:550-552](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/executor/execReplication.c#L550-L552), [worker.c:2723](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/replication/logical/worker.c#L2723), [worker.c:2753](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/replication/logical/worker.c#L2753)). The origin-based types need the local row's commit origin, which exists only when `track_commit_timestamp` is on ([conflict.c#GetTupleTransactionInfo](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/replication/logical/conflict.c#L62-L85), [logical-replication.sgml#conflict-update-origin-differs](../raw/postgres-18/doc/src/sgml/logical-replication.sgml#L1778-L1789)). `track_commit_timestamp` has context `postmaster`, so turning it on needs a restart ([guc_tables.c#track_commit_timestamp](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L1099-L1107)). Detection adds no configurable resolution. Key clashes such as `insert_exists` still raise an error until someone fixes the row by hand, missing rows are skipped, and origin-differs changes are applied anyway ([logical-replication.sgml#logical-replication-conflicts](../raw/postgres-18/doc/src/sgml/logical-replication.sgml#L1765-L1835)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Not present in PostgreSQL 12. The logical replication makefile builds no `conflict.o` ([logical/Makefile#OBJS](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/replication/logical/Makefile#L17-L18)). The docs only say that a constraint violation stops replication and that missing rows are skipped ([logical-replication.sgml#logical-replication-conflicts](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/logical-replication.sgml#L308-L318)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Not present in PostgreSQL 14 ([logical/Makefile#OBJS](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/replication/logical/Makefile#L17-L29), [logical-replication.sgml#logical-replication-conflicts](../raw/postgres-14/doc/src/sgml/logical-replication.sgml#L320-L330)).
- PostgreSQL 17: Not present in PostgreSQL 17 ([logical/Makefile#OBJS](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/replication/logical/Makefile#L17-L31), [logical-replication.sgml#logical-replication-conflicts](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/logical-replication.sgml#L1602-L1612)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds, except that 19 has an eighth type, `CT_UPDATE_DELETED`, for a row that another origin deleted concurrently ([conflict.h#ConflictType](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/replication/conflict.h#L31-L62)). It is detected only when `track_commit_timestamp` and the subscription option `retain_dead_tuples` are both on ([logical-replication.sgml#conflict-update-deleted](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/logical-replication.sgml#L2068-L2082), [pg_subscription.h:83-84](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/catalog/pg_subscription.h#L83-L84)). `ReportApplyConflict()` still counts and logs each conflict, and `track_commit_timestamp` is still `postmaster` context, so turning it on needs a restart ([conflict.c#ReportApplyConflict](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/replication/logical/conflict.c#L105-L133), [guc_parameters.dat:3199](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_parameters.dat#L3199)).

Related: [Logical replication](#logical-replication), [Apply worker](#apply-worker), [Replication origin](#replication-origin), [Subscription](#subscription), [Origin filter](#origin-filter)

### Constant folding

**Aliases:** `eval_const_expressions`, `estimate_expression_value`, expression simplification, const-simplification. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 17.

Constant folding is the [planner](#planner) computing parts of an expression that do not depend on any row, before the query runs, so `2 + 2` becomes `4`. `eval_const_expressions()` also simplifies boolean logic around unknown parts, turning `x OR true` into `true`. It evaluates only functions marked immutable, though it still folds their arguments ([clauses.c#eval_const_expressions](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L2223-L2259)). `preprocess_expression()` runs it on all of the query's expressions, function calls in `FROM` having had it earlier, because it also expands default arguments and named-argument calls, which the executor cannot handle ([planner.c#preprocess_expression-fold](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1183-L1202)).

A folded or inlined function leaves no trace in the plan, so the planner records it in `glob->invalItems` to know when the plan must be rebuilt ([clauses.c:2241-2244](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L2241-L2244)). A parameter value becomes a constant only when it is marked `PARAM_FLAG_CONST` ([clauses.c#eval_const_expressions_mutator-param](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L2461-L2497)). The plan cache asks its callers to set that flag for a custom plan, and the extended-query protocol's Bind message and PL/pgSQL both do ([plancache.c:903-906](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L903-L906), [postgres.c:1969-1973](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1969-L1973), [pl_exec.c:6413-6414](../raw/postgres-17/src/pl/plpgsql/src/pl_exec.c#L6413-L6414)). `estimate_expression_value()` is a looser variant used only for estimates: it also substitutes unmarked parameter values and folds stable functions ([clauses.c#estimate_expression_value](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L2387-L2416)).

Related: [SQL function inlining](#sql-function-inlining), [Function volatility](#function-volatility), [Custom and generic plan](#custom-and-generic-plan), [Planner support function](#planner-support-function), [Planner](#planner)

### Constraint exclusion

**Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

Constraint exclusion is a [planner](#planner) check that skips scanning a table when its restrictions cannot all be true. `relation_excluded_by_constraints()` excludes a relation whose `WHERE` restrictions contradict each other, or contradict its `CHECK` and `NOT NULL` constraints ([plancat.c#relation_excluded_by_constraints](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1569-L1600), [plancat.c:1659-1680](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1659-L1680), [plancat.c:1701-1709](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1701-L1709)). A constant `FALSE` or `NULL` restriction excludes the relation whatever the setting ([plancat.c:1603-1621](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1603-L1621)). The `constraint_exclusion` GUC controls the other tests. Its context is `user`, so a session or transaction can `SET` it with no reload or restart. Its default, `partition`, runs those tests only on appendrel members, such as inheritance children ([guc_tables.c#constraint_exclusion](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L4798-L4807), [plancat.c:1625-1641](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1625-L1641)). Do not confuse it with [partition pruning](#partition-pruning). Declarative partitions are pruned first from their partition bounds, so `partition` mode does not re-test their partition constraints ([plancat.c:1631-1638](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1631-L1638)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds, except for two details. The constant `FALSE` test fires only when that constant is the relation's single restriction clause, and `partition` mode also treats an inherited `UPDATE`/`DELETE` target as an appendrel member, because 12 still plans those through `inheritance_planner` ([plancat.c:1412-1429](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1412-L1429), [plancat.c:1441-1458](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1441-L1458)). The self-contradiction and constraint tests are the same, and `constraint_exclusion` is `PGC_USERSET` (session scope) with default `partition` ([plancat.c#relation_excluded_by_constraints](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1380-L1392), [plancat.c:1477-1498](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1477-L1498), [plancat.c:1519-1527](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1519-L1527), [guc.c#constraint_exclusion](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/utils/misc/guc.c#L4243-L4251)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds, except that the constant `FALSE` test still fires only when that constant is the relation's single restriction clause ([plancat.c:1517-1534](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1517-L1534)). The `off`/`partition`/`on` switch, the self-contradiction and constraint tests, and the `partition` rule that skips re-testing partition constraints are the same ([plancat.c:1541-1568](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1541-L1568), [plancat.c:1572-1593](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1572-L1593), [plancat.c:1614-1622](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1614-L1622)). `constraint_exclusion` is `PGC_USERSET` (session scope) with default `partition`, defined in `guc.c` ([guc.c#constraint_exclusion](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/utils/misc/guc.c#L4679-L4688)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds. Every restriction clause is still checked for a constant `FALSE`, the other tests are unchanged, and `constraint_exclusion` is still `user` context (session scope) with default `partition` ([plancat.c:1632-1650](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1632-L1650), [plancat.c:1654-1670](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1654-L1670), [plancat.c:1688-1709](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1688-L1709), [plancat.c:1732-1740](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1732-L1740), [guc_tables.c#constraint_exclusion](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L5061-L5070)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds. `relation_excluded_by_constraints()` still checks every clause for a constant `FALSE`, still refutes self-contradictory restrictions and constraint conflicts, and its `partition` mode still handles only appendrel members because pruning has already run ([plancat.c:1851-1869](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1851-L1869), [plancat.c:1874-1890](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1874-L1890), [plancat.c:1907-1928](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1907-L1928), [plancat.c:1951-1959](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1951-L1959)). `constraint_exclusion` is still `PGC_USERSET` (session scope) with default `partition` ([guc_parameters.dat#constraint_exclusion](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_parameters.dat#L526-L533)).

Related: [Partition pruning](#partition-pruning), [Planner](#planner), [RelOptInfo](#reloptinfo)

### Contrib

**Aliases:** `contrib/`, additional supplied modules. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

Contrib is the source directory of optional modules that ship with PostgreSQL but are not part of the core server ([contrib.sgml:7-15](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/contrib.sgml#L7-L15), [README:1-9](../raw/postgres-17/contrib/README#L1-L9)). A contrib module that adds SQL functions, operators or types is an [extension](#extension): it ships a `.control` file and is installed per database with `CREATE EXTENSION` ([README:19-25](../raw/postgres-17/contrib/README#L19-L25), [pageinspect.control:1-5](../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pageinspect/pageinspect.control#L1-L5)). Other modules are only loadable libraries. For example, `auto_explain` provides no SQL-accessible functions and is loaded with `LOAD` rather than `CREATE EXTENSION` ([auto-explain.sgml:18-23](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/auto-explain.sgml#L18-L23)). So "contrib module" and "extension" are not the same thing when reading source or docs.

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds. `contrib/` holds optional modules outside the core server, modules that add SQL objects are installed with `CREATE EXTENSION`, and `auto_explain` is loaded with `LOAD` ([contrib.sgml:6-15](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/contrib.sgml#L6-L15), [README:1-25](../raw/postgres-12/contrib/README#L1-L25), [auto-explain.sgml:23](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/auto-explain.sgml#L23)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds. The README and docs describe the same optional modules, modules that add SQL objects register with `CREATE EXTENSION`, and `auto_explain` is loaded with `LOAD` ([README:1-9](../raw/postgres-14/contrib/README#L1-L9), [README:18-25](../raw/postgres-14/contrib/README#L18-L25), [contrib.sgml:7-15](../raw/postgres-14/doc/src/sgml/contrib.sgml#L7-L15), [pageinspect.control:1-5](../raw/postgres-14/contrib/pageinspect/pageinspect.control#L1-L5), [auto-explain.sgml:23](../raw/postgres-14/doc/src/sgml/auto-explain.sgml#L23)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds ([contrib.sgml:7-15](../raw/postgres-18/doc/src/sgml/contrib.sgml#L7-L15), [README:1-9](../raw/postgres-18/contrib/README#L1-L9), [pageinspect.control:1-5](../raw/postgres-18/contrib/pageinspect/pageinspect.control#L1-L5), [auto-explain.sgml:18-23](../raw/postgres-18/doc/src/sgml/auto-explain.sgml#L18-L23)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds. The README and appendix wording and the `CREATE EXTENSION` path are unchanged, and `auto_explain` is still loaded with `LOAD` ([contrib.sgml:7-16](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/contrib.sgml#L7-L16), [README:1-28](../raw/postgres-19/contrib/README#L1-L28), [pageinspect.control:1-5](../raw/postgres-19/contrib/pageinspect/pageinspect.control#L1-L5), [auto-explain.sgml:18-24](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/auto-explain.sgml#L18-L24)). 19 also ships `pg_plan_advice`, another module that is loaded rather than installed with `CREATE EXTENSION` ([pgplanadvice.sgml#pgplanadvice-getting-started](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/pgplanadvice.sgml#L31-L39)).

Related: [Extension](#extension), [pageinspect](#pageinspect), [pgstattuple](#pgstattuple), [pg_freespacemap](#pg_freespacemap), [Hook](#hook)

### Control file

**Aliases:** `pg_control`, `global/pg_control`, `XLOG_CONTROL_FILE`, `ControlFileData`, `PG_CONTROL_VERSION`, `pg_controldata`. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 19.

In PostgreSQL 19, the control file is the small binary file `global/pg_control`, relative to the data directory, that records cluster-wide state such as format versions and the last checkpoint ([xlog_internal.h:146-149](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/access/xlog_internal.h#L146-L149)). Its layout is `ControlFileData`: the system identifier, the `pg_control_version` and `catalog_version_no` format stamps, the cluster state, the latest [checkpoint](#checkpoint) location with a copy of that checkpoint record, `minRecoveryPoint` and the backup fields, the WAL-related settings, build parameters such as block size and alignment, and a CRC that must come last ([pg_control.h#ControlFileData](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/catalog/pg_control.h#L105-L136), [pg_control.h:169-209](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/catalog/pg_control.h#L169-L209), [pg_control.h:246-248](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/catalog/pg_control.h#L246-L248)). The used part must stay within 512 bytes so that each update is an atomic write, and the file on disk is padded to 8192 bytes ([pg_control.h:250-265](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/catalog/pg_control.h#L250-L265)). `PG_CONTROL_VERSION` is 1905 at the pin, and `ReadControlFile()` stops startup when the stored format version, the CRC or the [catalog version](#catalog-version) does not match the binary ([pg_control.h:24-25](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/catalog/pg_control.h#L24-L25), [xlog.c#ReadControlFile](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L4446-L4498)). `BootStrapXLOG()` creates the file with `WriteControlFile()`, and `UpdateControlFile()` rewrites and flushes it through the shared `update_controlfile()` routine ([xlog.c:5287-5288](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5287-L5288), [xlog.c#UpdateControlFile](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L4636-L4644), [controldata_utils.c#update_controlfile](../raw/postgres-19/src/common/controldata_utils.c#L180-L200)). Two fields hold the [data checksums](#data-checksums) state: `data_checksum_version` is the current state, and `data_checksum_version_init` keeps the state from cluster initialization, which `pg_control_init()` returns as `data_page_checksum_version` ([pg_control.h:224-231](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/catalog/pg_control.h#L224-L231), [pg_controldata.c#pg_control_init](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/misc/pg_controldata.c#L206-L258)). The `pg_controldata` program prints the file, and the SQL functions `pg_control_system()`, `pg_control_checkpoint()`, `pg_control_recovery()` and `pg_control_init()` return most of the same fields ([pg_controldata.sgml#r1-app-pgcontroldata-1](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/ref/pg_controldata.sgml#L36-L44), [func-info.sgml#functions-info-controldata](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/func/func-info.sgml#L3295-L3306), [pg_controldata.c:32](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/misc/pg_controldata.c#L32), [pg_controldata.c:70](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/misc/pg_controldata.c#L70), [pg_controldata.c:166](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/misc/pg_controldata.c#L166)). An extension's `.control` file is a different thing; see [Extension](#extension).

Related: [Catalog version](#catalog-version), [Checkpoint](#checkpoint), [Crash recovery](#crash-recovery), [Data checksums](#data-checksums), [XLOG_PAGE_MAGIC](#xlog_page_magic), [Extension](#extension)

### Correlation

**Aliases:** `pg_stats.correlation`, `STATISTIC_KIND_CORRELATION`, physical-order correlation, `indexCorrelation`. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

Correlation is a per-column [statistic](#statistics) between −1 and +1. It measures how closely the table's physical row order follows the column's sorted order ([pg_statistic.h#STATISTIC_KIND_CORRELATION](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/pg_statistic.h#L212-L222)). `ANALYZE` computes it with the other scalar statistics, and the `pg_stats` view shows it as the `correlation` column ([analyze.c:2807-2834](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L2807-L2834), [system_views.sql:219-225](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/system_views.sql#L219-L225)). It matters for index scan costing. `cost_index()` computes a best case, where matching rows sit on consecutive heap pages, and a worst case, where every heap page fetch is random. It then blends the two by the square of the correlation ([costsize.c#cost_index](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L730-L746), [costsize.c:785-787](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L785-L787)). For a B-tree, `btcostestimate()` takes the value from the leading index column's statistics and scales it by 0.75 for a multicolumn index ([selfuncs.c:7108-7124](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L7108-L7124), [selfuncs.c#btcostestimate](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L7182-L7199)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds. The statistic kind, the `ANALYZE` step, the `pg_stats` column, the `cost_index()` blend and the leading-column rule with its 0.75 factor are the same ([pg_statistic.h#STATISTIC_KIND_CORRELATION](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/catalog/pg_statistic.h#L201-L210), [analyze.c:2613](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L2613), [system_views.sql:219-225](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/catalog/system_views.sql#L219-L225), [costsize.c:712-714](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L712-L714), [selfuncs.c:6119-6124](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L6119-L6124)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds ([pg_statistic.h#STATISTIC_KIND_CORRELATION](../raw/postgres-14/src/include/catalog/pg_statistic.h#L209-L218), [analyze.c:2862](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L2862), [system_views.sql:219-225](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/catalog/system_views.sql#L219-L225), [costsize.c:727-729](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L727-L729), [selfuncs.c:6902-6907](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L6902-L6907)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds, except that the 0.75 rule moved out of `btcostestimate()` into a new static helper, `btcost_correlation()`, which `btcostestimate()` calls ([selfuncs.c#btcost_correlation](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L7319-L7330), [selfuncs.c:7811-7813](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L7811-L7813)). The statistic kind, the `ANALYZE` step, the `pg_stats` column and the `cost_index()` blend are unchanged ([pg_statistic.h#STATISTIC_KIND_CORRELATION](../raw/postgres-18/src/include/catalog/pg_statistic.h#L213-L222), [analyze.c:2853](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L2853), [system_views.sql:215-221](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/catalog/system_views.sql#L215-L221), [costsize.c:795-797](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L795-L797)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds, except that, as in 18, the 0.75 rule lives in `btcost_correlation()`, which `btcostestimate()` calls ([selfuncs.c#btcost_correlation](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L7666-L7677), [selfuncs.c:8167-8169](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L8167-L8169)). The other parts are unchanged ([pg_statistic.h#STATISTIC_KIND_CORRELATION](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/catalog/pg_statistic.h#L217-L226), [analyze.c:2917](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L2917), [system_views.sql:222-228](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/catalog/system_views.sql#L222-L228), [costsize.c:784-786](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L784-L786)).

### Cost

**Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

A cost is the [planner](#planner)'s estimate of how expensive a plan step is. Costs use arbitrary units set by a few base parameters, conventionally scaled so that `seq_page_cost`, one sequential page read, is 1.0 ([costsize.c:6-30](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6-L30), [config.sgml:5810-5820](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/config.sgml#L5810-L5820)). Every [path](#path) carries a `startup_cost`, spent before the first row, and a `total_cost`, spent to fetch all rows ([pathnodes.h#Path](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1662-L1665), [costsize.c:37-46](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L37-L46)). The C type `Cost` is a `double` ([nodes.h:251](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/nodes.h#L251)). The base parameters (`seq_page_cost`, `random_page_cost`, `cpu_tuple_cost`, `cpu_index_tuple_cost`, `cpu_operator_cost`) are globals in `costsize.c` ([costsize.c:119-128](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L119-L128)). Each index access method prices its own scans through its `amcostestimate` callback ([costsize.c#cost_index](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L610-L621)). A plan type disabled by a setting such as `enable_seqscan = off` is not removed: 17 adds `disable_cost`, 1.0e10, to the path's startup cost, so the path loses unless nothing else is possible ([costsize.c:130](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L130), [costsize.c:304-305](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L304-L305)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds. Costs use the same arbitrary units, each path has `startup_cost` and `total_cost`, `Cost` is a `double`, the base parameters are globals, `cost_index()` calls the AM's `amcostestimate`, and a disabled plan type gets `disable_cost` ([costsize.c:6-14](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6-L14), [pathnodes.h#Path](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1121-L1122), [nodes.h:658](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/nodes/nodes.h#L658), [costsize.c:110-114](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L110-L114), [costsize.c:544](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L544), [costsize.c:120](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L120), [costsize.c:231-232](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L231-L232)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds. Paths carry `startup_cost` and `total_cost`, `Cost` is a `double`, the base cost parameters are globals in `costsize.c`, `cost_index()` calls the AM's `amcostestimate`, and a disabled plan type gets `disable_cost` ([pathnodes.h#Path](../raw/postgres-14/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1191-L1192), [nodes.h:673](../raw/postgres-14/src/include/nodes/nodes.h#L673), [costsize.c:119-123](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L119-L123), [costsize.c#cost_index](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L559-L561), [costsize.c:129](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L129), [costsize.c:246-247](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L246-L247)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Differs: a disabled plan type no longer gets `disable_cost`. A `Path` now carries `disabled_nodes`, a count of disabled plan nodes, such as a seq scan under `enable_seqscan = off` ([pathnodes.h#Path](../raw/postgres-18/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1794-L1797), [costsize.c:357](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L357)). `add_path()` treats that count as a higher-order part of the cost, so startup and total cost only break ties between paths with equal counts ([pathnode.c#add_path](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L401-L411)). `disable_cost` remains only for a hash join whose inner bucket would overflow hash memory ([costsize.c:4411-4421](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4411-L4421)). The cost units, `Cost` type, base parameters and `amcostestimate` are unchanged ([costsize.c:6-30](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6-L30), [nodes.h:257](../raw/postgres-18/src/include/nodes/nodes.h#L257), [costsize.c:130-139](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L130-L139)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Differs, as in 18: paths count `disabled_nodes`, and `add_path()` ranks that count above `startup_cost` and `total_cost` ([pathnodes.h#Path](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L2004-L2008), [pathnode.c#add_path](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L395-L405)). In 19 the count comes from the rel's [pgs_mask](#pgs_mask) rather than straight from the `enable_*` settings ([costsize.c:335-336](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L335-L336), [costsize.c:603-607](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L603-L607)). Costs are still arbitrary units, `Cost` is still a `double`, the base parameters are still globals, and `cost_index()` still calls the AM's `amcostestimate` ([costsize.c:6-40](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6-L40), [nodes.h:259](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/nodes/nodes.h#L259), [costsize.c:131-140](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L131-L140), [costsize.c#cost_index](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L616-L620)).

Related: [Path](#path), [Planner](#planner), [Selectivity](#selectivity), [effective_cache_size](#effective_cache_size), [pgs_mask](#pgs_mask)

### Covering index

**Aliases:** `INCLUDE` columns, non-key columns, `indnkeyatts`, `amcaninclude`. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

A covering index holds every column that a frequent query needs, so an [index-only scan](#index-only-scan) can answer the query without visiting the table. `CREATE INDEX ... INCLUDE (...)` adds such payload columns, called non-key columns, next to the key columns ([indices.sgml#indexes-index-only-scans](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/indices.sgml#L1201-L1209)). Searches cannot use non-key columns, and uniqueness ignores them, but an index-only scan can return them ([ref/create_index.sgml:153-165](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L153-L165)). [pg_index](#pg_index) records the split: `indnatts` counts all columns and `indnkeyatts` counts only the key columns ([pg_index.h#FormData_pg_index](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/pg_index.h#L30-L35)). An [access method](#access-method) opts in with `amcaninclude`. In PostgreSQL 17, B-tree, GiST and SP-GiST set it ([nbtree.c:121](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtree.c#L121), [gist.c:79](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/gist/gist.c#L79), [spgutils.c:64](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/spgist/spgutils.c#L64)). Non-key columns widen every index tuple. A B-tree with any `INCLUDE` column never uses [deduplication](#deduplication), because `_bt_allequalimage()` returns false for it ([ref/create_index.sgml:167-174](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L167-L174), [nbtutils.c#_bt_allequalimage](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtutils.c#L5140-L5147)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds, except that only B-tree and GiST support `INCLUDE` (SP-GiST sets `amcaninclude = false`) and B-tree deduplication does not exist yet, so the deduplication rule does not apply ([nbtree.c:125](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtree.c#L125), [gist.c:77](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/access/gist/gist.c#L77), [spgutils.c:58](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/access/spgist/spgutils.c#L58), [nbtree.h#BTMetaPageData](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/access/nbtree.h#L97-L110)). The covering-index docs, `INCLUDE` and `indnkeyatts` are the same ([indices.sgml#indexes-index-only-scans](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/indices.sgml#L1120-L1128), [ref/create_index.sgml:153-165](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_index.sgml#L153-L165), [pg_index.h:34](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/catalog/pg_index.h#L34)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds. SP-GiST supports `INCLUDE` as well, and `_bt_allequalimage()` rejects `INCLUDE` indexes ([indices.sgml#indexes-index-only-scans](../raw/postgres-14/doc/src/sgml/indices.sgml#L1199-L1207), [spgutils.c:63](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/access/spgist/spgutils.c#L63), [nbtutils.c:2717](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtutils.c#L2717)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds ([indices.sgml#indexes-index-only-scans](../raw/postgres-18/doc/src/sgml/indices.sgml#L1241-L1249), [nbtree.c:138](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtree.c#L138), [gist.c:82](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/gist/gist.c#L82), [spgutils.c:67](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/spgist/spgutils.c#L67), [nbtutils.c:4264](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtutils.c#L4264)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds ([indices.sgml#indexes-index-only-scans](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/indices.sgml#L1241-L1249), [nbtree.c:141](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtree.c#L141), [gist.c:82](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/gist/gist.c#L82), [spgutils.c:67](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/spgist/spgutils.c#L67), [nbtutils.c:1180](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtutils.c#L1180)).

Related: [Index-only scan](#index-only-scan), [pg_index](#pg_index), [Deduplication](#deduplication), [B-tree](#b-tree)

### Crash recovery

**Aliases:** WAL replay, redo. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

Crash recovery is the startup step that replays [WAL](#wal) from the last [checkpoint](#checkpoint)'s redo point after an unclean shutdown. It re-applies every change that may not have reached the data files ([wal.sgml#wal-configuration](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/wal.sgml#L502-L505)). `InitWalRecovery()` sets `InRecovery` when the control file shows an unclean shutdown. It also sets it after a clean shutdown when a `standby.signal` or `recovery.signal` file requests archive recovery ([xlogrecovery.c:911-928](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L911-L928), [xlogrecovery.c:1095-1104](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L1095-L1104)). `StartupXLOG()` then calls `PerformWalRecovery()`, so the same replay loop serves crash recovery, archive recovery and standby mode ([xlog.c:5647](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5647), [xlog.c:5802](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5802)). `PerformWalRecovery()` therefore does run after a clean shutdown when a signal file is present, although its header comment says it never does ([xlogrecovery.c#PerformWalRecovery](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L1656-L1662)). Each record goes to its resource manager's `rm_redo` callback ([xlogrecovery.c#ApplyWalRecord](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L1997-L2001)). Redo compares the page [LSN](#lsn) with the record's position to skip changes already applied ([transam/README:420-422](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/README#L420-L422)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds, except that 12 has no `xlogrecovery.c`, `InitWalRecovery()` or `PerformWalRecovery()`. `StartupXLOG()` in `xlog.c` sets `InRecovery` itself, including after a clean shutdown when a signal file requests recovery, and runs the replay loop that calls each record's `rm_redo` ([xlog.c:6729-6746](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L6729-L6746), [xlog.c:5355-5364](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5355-L5364), [xlog.c:7183](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L7183)). Recovery replays WAL from the latest checkpoint's redo record, and redo uses the page LSN to skip changes already applied ([wal.sgml#wal-configuration](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/wal.sgml#L454-L457), [transam/README:411-413](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/access/transam/README#L411-L413)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds, except that, as in 12, `StartupXLOG()` in `xlog.c` does the work that 17 splits into `xlogrecovery.c`. It sets `InRecovery` after an unclean shutdown or when a signal file requests recovery, and its replay loop calls each record's `rm_redo` ([xlog.c:7101-7118](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L7101-L7118), [xlog.c:5558-5567](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5558-L5567), [xlog.c:7575-7576](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L7575-L7576)). Replay starts at the redo record, and redo still skips changes by comparing the page LSN ([wal.sgml#wal-configuration](../raw/postgres-14/doc/src/sgml/wal.sgml#L501-L504), [transam/README:420-422](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/access/transam/README#L420-L422)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds. `InitWalRecovery()` still forces `InRecovery` for a signal file after a clean shutdown, `StartupXLOG()` still calls `PerformWalRecovery()`, and each record still goes to `rm_redo` ([xlogrecovery.c:929-946](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L929-L946), [xlogrecovery.c:1113-1122](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L1113-L1122), [xlog.c:5886](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5886), [xlogrecovery.c#ApplyWalRecord](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L2016-L2020)). The docs, the stale header comment and the page-LSN rule are unchanged ([wal.sgml#wal-configuration](../raw/postgres-18/doc/src/sgml/wal.sgml#L500-L503), [xlogrecovery.c#PerformWalRecovery](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L1674-L1680), [transam/README:420-422](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/transam/README#L420-L422)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds. Replay still starts from the latest checkpoint's redo record, and `InitWalRecovery()` still forces `InRecovery` after a clean shutdown when a signal file requests recovery, so `PerformWalRecovery()` still runs in that case despite its header comment ([wal.sgml#wal-configuration](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/wal.sgml#L506-L509), [xlogrecovery.c:867-884](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L867-L884), [xlogrecovery.c:1053-1062](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L1053-L1062), [xlog.c:5962](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5962), [xlogrecovery.c#PerformWalRecovery](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L1615-L1621)). Each record still goes to its resource manager's `rm_redo`, and redo still skips changes whose page LSN is already past the record ([xlogrecovery.c:1975](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlogrecovery.c#L1975), [transam/README:420-422](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/README#L420-L422)).

Related: [Checkpoint](#checkpoint), [Full-page image](#full-page-image), [LSN](#lsn), [WAL](#wal)

### Critical section

**Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

A critical section is a stretch of backend code in which any `ERROR` or `FATAL` becomes a `PANIC`, forcing a system-wide reset, and in which cancel and die interrupts are held off ([miscadmin.h:79-84](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/miscadmin.h#L79-L84)). `START_CRIT_SECTION()` and `END_CRIT_SECTION()` just raise and lower the counter `CritSectionCount` ([miscadmin.h#START_CRIT_SECTION](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/miscadmin.h#L150-L156)). While that counter is non-zero, `errstart()` promotes every level from `ERROR` up to `PANIC`, and `ProcessInterrupts()` returns without acting ([elog.c#errstart](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/error/elog.c#L357-L364), [postgres.c:3275](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L3275)). WAL-logged page changes are wrapped in one: shared buffers then hold changes that are not yet logged, and an ordinary error must not let those changes reach disk ([transam/README:442-446](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/README#L442-L446)). It is not a lock. The macros only change a counter in the current backend, so other processes are not blocked ([miscadmin.h#START_CRIT_SECTION](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/miscadmin.h#L150-L156)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds. The header comment, the counter macros, the promotion to `PANIC` in `errstart()`, the interrupt holdoff and the WAL-logging rule are the same ([miscadmin.h:70-75](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/miscadmin.h#L70-L75), [miscadmin.h#START_CRIT_SECTION](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/miscadmin.h#L132-L138), [elog.c#errstart](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/utils/error/elog.c#L246-L249), [postgres.c:2955](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L2955), [transam/README:433-437](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/access/transam/README#L433-L437)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds ([miscadmin.h:79-84](../raw/postgres-14/src/include/miscadmin.h#L79-L84), [miscadmin.h#START_CRIT_SECTION](../raw/postgres-14/src/include/miscadmin.h#L148-L154), [elog.c#errstart](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/utils/error/elog.c#L355-L358), [postgres.c:3138](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L3138), [transam/README:441-446](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/access/transam/README#L441-L446)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds ([miscadmin.h:79-84](../raw/postgres-18/src/include/miscadmin.h#L79-L84), [miscadmin.h#START_CRIT_SECTION](../raw/postgres-18/src/include/miscadmin.h#L150-L156), [elog.c#errstart](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/error/elog.c#L353-L361), [postgres.c:3302](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L3302), [transam/README:442-446](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/transam/README#L442-L446)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds. `START_CRIT_SECTION()` and `END_CRIT_SECTION()` still only change `CritSectionCount`, `errstart()` still promotes errors to `PANIC` inside one, interrupts are still held off, and the README still wraps WAL-logged page changes in one ([miscadmin.h:79-84](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/miscadmin.h#L79-L84), [miscadmin.h#START_CRIT_SECTION](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/miscadmin.h#L152-L158), [elog.c#errstart](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/error/elog.c#L366-L373), [postgres.c:3365](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L3365), [transam/README:442-446](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/README#L442-L446)).

Related: [WAL](#wal), [ereport](#ereport)

### Cumulative statistics

**Aliases:** cumulative statistics system, pgstat, collected statistics views. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

The cumulative statistics system counts server activity: table and index accesses, row counts, and vacuum and analyze runs ([monitoring.sgml#monitoring-stats](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/monitoring.sgml#L137-L145)). In `pgstat.c`, each process accumulates counters locally as pending entries and later flushes them to shared memory through `pgstat_report_stat()` ([pgstat.c:44-50](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L44-L50)). The startup process loads the stats from disk. After a crash, or after an immediate shutdown, which startup treats as a crash, it discards them instead ([pgstat.c:12-15](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L12-L15), [xlog.c:5503-5511](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5503-L5511), [xlog.c:5636-5639](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5636-L5639)). The [checkpointer](#checkpointer) writes the stats file only at a clean shutdown ([checkpointer.c:223](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/postmaster/checkpointer.c#L223), [pgstat.c:478-487](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L478-L487)). The `track_counts` GUC switches collection. Its context is `superuser` (`PGC_SUSET`), so a superuser can change it per session ([guc_tables.c#track_counts](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L1412-L1419)). The collected statistics views, such as `pg_stat_database` and `pg_stat_all_tables`, show these counters. The dynamic views, such as `pg_stat_activity`, show what processes are doing right now and are a separate facility ([monitoring.sgml#monitoring-stats](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/monitoring.sgml#L147-L152), [monitoring.sgml:307-314](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/monitoring.sgml#L307-L314), [monitoring.sgml:464-467](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/monitoring.sgml#L464-L467), [monitoring.sgml:527-532](../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/monitoring.sgml#L527-L532)). Do not confuse these activity counters with the planner's column [statistics](#statistics).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Differs: 12 has a separate statistics collector process, not a shared-memory system. Backends send counters over a UDP socket with `pgstat_report_stat()`, and the collector writes files under `stats_temp_directory` ([pgstat.c:1-16](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L1-L16), [pgstat.c:420-424](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L420-L424), [pgstat.c#pgstat_report_stat](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L803-L813)). The collector saves its permanent stats file when it exits. `StartupXLOG()` deletes the stats whenever it performs recovery, so they are lost after a crash or an immediate shutdown, and also after archive recovery or a standby start ([pgstat.c:4676-4678](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L4676-L4678), [xlog.c:6749](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L6749), [xlog.c:6843-6846](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L6843-L6846)). The docs call it "the statistics collector" and keep the live activity view separate ([monitoring.sgml#monitoring-stats](../raw/postgres-12/doc/src/sgml/monitoring.sgml#L132-L155)). `track_counts` is `PGC_SUSET` (superuser, session scope), and `stats_temp_directory` is `PGC_SIGHUP`, so changing it needs a reload ([guc.c#track_counts](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/utils/misc/guc.c#L1393-L1400), [guc.c#stats_temp_directory](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/utils/misc/guc.c#L4076-L4079)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Differs: as in 12, 14 uses a separate statistics collector process that receives UDP messages from backends and writes stats files; the shared-memory system does not exist yet ([pgstat.c:1-17](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L1-L17), [pgstat.c:404-406](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L404-L406), [monitoring.sgml#monitoring-stats](../raw/postgres-14/doc/src/sgml/monitoring.sgml#L138-L154)). `pgstat_report_stat()` sends table stats as messages ([pgstat.c:844](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L844)). The collector saves the permanent stats file when it exits, and `StartupXLOG()` deletes the stats after any recovery ([pgstat.c:3451-3453](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L3451-L3453), [xlog.c:7127](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L7127), [xlog.c:7231-7234](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L7231-L7234)). `track_counts` is `PGC_SUSET` (superuser, session scope) ([guc.c:1527](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/utils/misc/guc.c#L1527)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds, except for two additions. A statistics kind can opt out of the stats file with the new `write_to_file` flag, and extensions can register custom statistics kinds at startup with `pgstat_register_kind()` ([pgstat.c:12-16](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L12-L16), [pgstat_internal.h:217](../raw/postgres-18/src/include/utils/pgstat_internal.h#L217), [pgstat.c:53-62](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L53-L62), [pgstat.c:1465](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L1465)). Pending counters are still flushed through `pgstat_report_stat()`, the checkpointer still writes the file only at a clean shutdown, and the stats are still discarded after a crash ([pgstat.c:45-51](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L45-L51), [checkpointer.c:232](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/postmaster/checkpointer.c#L232), [pgstat.c:576-585](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L576-L585), [xlog.c:5587-5595](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5587-L5595), [xlog.c:5720-5723](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5720-L5723)). `track_counts` is still `PGC_SUSET` (superuser, session scope) ([guc_tables.c#track_counts](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L1495-L1502)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds, except that, as in 18, a statistics kind can opt out of the stats file and extensions can register custom kinds ([pgstat.c:12-16](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L12-L16), [pgstat_internal.h:246](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/utils/pgstat_internal.h#L246), [pgstat.c:53-55](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L53-L55)). Processes still keep pending entries and flush them with `pgstat_report_stat()`, the checkpointer still writes the stats at a clean shutdown, and they are still discarded after a crash ([monitoring.sgml#monitoring-stats](../raw/postgres-19/doc/src/sgml/monitoring.sgml#L137-L152), [pgstat.c:45-51](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L45-L51), [checkpointer.c:254](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/postmaster/checkpointer.c#L254), [pgstat.c:606-615](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L606-L615), [xlog.c:5659-5667](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5659-L5667), [xlog.c:5797-5800](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L5797-L5800)). `track_counts` is still `PGC_SUSET` (session scope, superuser only) ([guc_parameters.dat#track_counts](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_parameters.dat#L3211-L3215)).

Related: [Statistics](#statistics), [Cumulative statistics kind](#cumulative-statistics-kind), [Shared-memory statistics](#shared-memory-statistics), [pg_stat_all_tables](#pg_stat_all_tables), [Wait event](#wait-event), [GUC context](#guc-context)

### Cumulative statistics kind

**Aliases:** `PgStat_Kind`, `PgStat_KindInfo`, stats kind, custom cumulative statistics, `pgstat_register_kind`, fixed-numbered and variable-numbered stats. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

A statistics kind is one category of [cumulative statistics](#cumulative-statistics), such as the per-table counters or the checkpointer's counters. PostgreSQL 17 lists its kinds in the `PgStat_Kind` enum. Variable-numbered kinds keep one entry per object (database, relation, function, replication slot, subscription). Fixed-numbered kinds keep a fixed number of entries, most commonly one (archiver, bgwriter, checkpointer, I/O, SLRU, WAL) ([pgstat.h#PgStat_Kind](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/pgstat.h#L33-L54), [pgstat.c:5-10](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L5-L10)). Each kind has a `PgStat_KindInfo` descriptor. Its `fixed_amount` flag records which group the kind is in, and the table `pgstat_kind_infos[]` holds one descriptor per kind ([pgstat_internal.h#PgStat_KindInfo](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/pgstat_internal.h#L201-L219), [pgstat.c:258](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L258)). In 17 the list is a closed C enum, with no registration call for extensions ([pgstat.h#PgStat_Kind](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/pgstat.h#L33-L54)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Not present in PostgreSQL 12. Statistics flow through a separate statistics collector process in `postmaster/pgstat.c`, not through a kind registry ([pgstat.c:2-4](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L2-L4)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Not present in PostgreSQL 14. It still uses the statistics collector process ([pgstat.c:1-6](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L1-L6)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Differs: `PgStat_Kind` becomes a `uint32` ID. Built-in kinds use IDs 1 to 12, including a new per-backend kind, and IDs 24 to 32 are reserved for custom kinds ([pgstat_kind.h:16-59](../raw/postgres-18/src/include/utils/pgstat_kind.h#L16-L59)). An extension registers a custom kind with `pgstat_register_kind()`, which must run while `shared_preload_libraries` loads ([pgstat.c#pgstat_register_kind](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L1455-L1483)). `shared_preload_libraries` has context `postmaster`, so adding such an extension needs a restart ([guc_tables.c#shared_preload_libraries](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L4487-L4488)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Differs, as in 18: kinds are `uint32` IDs, extensions register custom kinds with `pgstat_register_kind()`, and `shared_preload_libraries` is still `postmaster` context, so adding such an extension needs a restart ([pgstat.c#pgstat_register_kind](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat.c#L1508-L1522), [guc_parameters.dat:2746](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_parameters.dat#L2746)). 19 also adds a fixed-numbered lock kind, so built-in IDs run 1 to 13 ([pgstat_kind.h:26-52](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/utils/pgstat_kind.h#L26-L52)).

Related: [Cumulative statistics](#cumulative-statistics), [Shared-memory statistics](#shared-memory-statistics), [shared_preload_libraries](#shared_preload_libraries), [Extension](#extension)

### Custom and generic plan

**Aliases:** plan cache, cached plan, `CachedPlanSource`, `CachedPlan`, `plancache.c`, `choose_custom_plan`. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

A statement with parameters, such as a [prepared statement](#prepared-statement), can run with two kinds of plan. A custom plan is built for the actual parameter values of one execution. A generic plan is built once without those values and reused. The plan cache in `plancache.c` makes this choice and throws cached plans away when the objects they depend on change ([plancache.c:6-30](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L6-L30)). Each cached statement is a `CachedPlanSource`, which holds the generic plan and running cost totals for the custom plans ([plancache.h#CachedPlanSource](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/plancache.h#L121-L133)). `choose_custom_plan()` makes the decision. It picks the generic plan at once for a statement with no bound parameters and a custom plan for a one-shot plan. Otherwise it asks for custom plans for the first five executions, then prefers the generic plan when its cost is below the average custom-plan cost, which includes a planning charge ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1054-L1101)). The `plan_cache_mode` setting can force either kind. Its context is `user`, so it applies per session or transaction ([guc_tables.c#plan_cache_mode](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L5111-L5122)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds, including the five-custom-plan rule and `plan_cache_mode` with context `user` ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1016-L1063), [guc.c:4504](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/utils/misc/guc.c#L4504)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1031-L1078), [guc.c:4949](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/utils/misc/guc.c#L4949)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1166-L1213), [guc_tables.c:5385](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L5385)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1184-L1231), [guc_parameters.dat:2363](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_parameters.dat#L2363)).

Related: [Plan cache mode](#plan-cache-mode), [Prepared statement](#prepared-statement), [Planner](#planner), [Invalidation message](#invalidation-message), [SPI](#spi)

### Custom scan

**Aliases:** `CustomPath`, `CustomScan`, `CustomScanState`, `CustomPathMethods`, `CustomScanMethods`, `CustomExecMethods`, custom scan provider. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 17.

A custom scan is a way of scanning a table, or of joining tables, that an extension implements instead of core code. The comment on `CustomPath` gives GPU acceleration and cache-based scans as examples ([pathnodes.h#CustomPath-comment](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1878-L1886)). The extension adds a `CustomPath` to a base relation from `set_rel_pathlist_hook`, or to a join relation from `set_join_pathlist_hook` ([pathnodes.h#CustomPath-comment](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1888-L1890)).

The provider supplies three method tables. `CustomPathMethods.PlanCustomPath` turns the chosen path into a `CustomScan` plan node, which `create_customscan_plan()` calls after ordering the scan clauses ([extensible.h#CustomPathMethods](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/extensible.h#L92-L106), [createplan.c#create_customscan_plan](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L4294-L4310)). `CustomScanMethods` creates the executor state, and `CustomExecMethods` runs it ([extensible.h#CustomScanMethods](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/extensible.h#L112-L118), [extensible.h#CustomExecMethods](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/extensible.h#L124-L138)). Because plan trees are copied, a `CustomScan` must keep all its data in its own list fields ([plannodes.h#CustomScan-comment](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L731-L735)). Its `flags` declare backward-scan, mark-and-restore and projection support ([extensible.h:78-86](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/extensible.h#L78-L86)), and `RegisterCustomScanMethods()` registers the methods by name ([extensible.c#RegisterCustomScanMethods](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/extensible.c#L84-L94)).

Related: [Hook](#hook), [Path](#path), [Foreign data wrapper](#foreign-data-wrapper), [Executor](#executor), [Planner](#planner)

### Data checksums

**Aliases:** page checksum, `pd_checksum`, `data_checksums`, `initdb --data-checksums`, `pg_checksums`. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

Data checksums are a 16-bit value, stored in each data [page](#page) header, that lets PostgreSQL detect a page corrupted on disk. The field is `pd_checksum`, and it is left unset when checksums are off ([bufpage.h:127-134](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/storage/bufpage.h#L127-L134)). When checksums are on, `PageIsVerifiedExtended()` recomputes the checksum of every page read in and compares it with the stored value ([bufpage.c#PageIsVerifiedExtended](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/storage/page/bufpage.c#L88-L109)). The choice is made per cluster. In PostgreSQL 17, `initdb -k` turns checksums on and the default is off. The offline `pg_checksums` tool can enable, disable or check them on a stopped cluster ([initdb.c:167](../raw/postgres-17/src/bin/initdb/initdb.c#L167), [initdb.c:2511](../raw/postgres-17/src/bin/initdb/initdb.c#L2511), [pg_checksums.c:1-5](../raw/postgres-17/src/bin/pg_checksums/pg_checksums.c#L1-L5)). The read-only `data_checksums` setting reports the state; its context is `internal`, so no configuration change can set it ([guc_tables.c:1883-1890](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L1883-L1890)). Checksums cost extra WAL. The first hint-bit change to a page after a [checkpoint](#checkpoint), when no other WAL record has touched the page since, is logged as a [full-page image](#full-page-image); later hint-bit changes in that cycle are not logged. Without that image, a torn write could leave a page whose checksum no longer matches ([xlog.h#XLogHintBitIsNeeded](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/xlog.h#L110-L118), [xloginsert.c#XLogSaveBufferForHint](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/xloginsert.c#L1055-L1089)). `wal_log_hints` forces the same logging without checksums. Its context is `postmaster`, so changing it needs a restart ([guc_tables.c:1171](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L1171)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds, except that the verify function is `PageIsVerified()` and `data_checksums` is defined in `guc.c` ([bufpage.c:82](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/storage/page/bufpage.c#L82), [guc.c:1827](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/utils/misc/guc.c#L1827)). Checksums are off by default, hint bits are logged under the same first-change rule, and `pg_checksums` already works offline ([initdb.c:144](../raw/postgres-12/src/bin/initdb/initdb.c#L144), [xlog.h:192](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/access/xlog.h#L192), [xloginsert.c:917](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/access/transam/xloginsert.c#L917), [pg_checksums.c:1-5](../raw/postgres-12/src/bin/pg_checksums/pg_checksums.c#L1-L5)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds. Checksums are off by default, `PageIsVerifiedExtended()` verifies pages, and the hint-bit rule is the same ([initdb.c:146](../raw/postgres-14/src/bin/initdb/initdb.c#L146), [bufpage.c:88](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/storage/page/bufpage.c#L88), [guc.c:1991](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/utils/misc/guc.c#L1991), [xloginsert.c:941](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/access/transam/xloginsert.c#L941)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Differs: `initdb` turns checksums on by default, and `--no-data-checksums` turns them off ([initdb.c:167](../raw/postgres-18/src/bin/initdb/initdb.c#L167), [initdb.c:2542](../raw/postgres-18/src/bin/initdb/initdb.c#L2542)). Verification is `PageIsVerified()` again ([bufpage.c:94](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/storage/page/bufpage.c#L94)). The hint-bit rule is unchanged ([xloginsert.c:1089](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/access/transam/xloginsert.c#L1089)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Differs: as in 18, `initdb` turns checksums on by default and `PageIsVerified()` verifies pages ([initdb.c:167](../raw/postgres-19/src/bin/initdb/initdb.c#L167), [bufpage.c:94](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/storage/page/bufpage.c#L94)). `--no-data-checksums` turns them off ([initdb.c:2544](../raw/postgres-19/src/bin/initdb/initdb.c#L2544)). At the pinned 19beta4-era commit, checksums cannot be switched on or off in a running cluster: the online transition (`pg_enable_data_checksums()` and its worker) was reverted, and `data_checksums` is again a `bool` with context `internal` ([guc_parameters.dat#data_checksums](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_parameters.dat#L581-L586)). Hint-bit logging keys off `DataChecksumsEnabled()`, which reads the control file's `data_checksum_version`, as in 18 ([xlog.h#XLogHintBitIsNeeded](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/access/xlog.h#L135), [xlog.c#DataChecksumsEnabled](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L4669-L4674), [xloginsert.c:1161](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xloginsert.c#L1161)). The [control file](#control-file) also keeps the initdb-time state in `data_checksum_version_init`, which `pg_control_init()` reports as `data_page_checksum_version` ([pg_control.h:224-231](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/catalog/pg_control.h#L224-L231), [xlog.c:4294-4295](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/access/transam/xlog.c#L4294-L4295), [pg_controldata.c:257](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/misc/pg_controldata.c#L257)).

Related: [Page](#page), [Full-page image](#full-page-image), [WAL](#wal), [GUC context](#guc-context), [Control file](#control-file), [ProcSignal barrier](#procsignal-barrier)

### Datum

**Aliases:** `Datum`, `DatumGetX`, `XGetDatum`, `NullableDatum`, pass-by-value, pass-by-reference, `typbyval`. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

A `Datum` is the generic C type that backend code uses to hold one SQL value. It holds the value itself for a small pass-by-value type, or a pointer to the value for a pass-by-reference type. It is exactly as wide as a pointer ([postgres.h#Datum](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/postgres.h#L54-L64)). Code converts with paired helpers such as `DatumGetInt32()` and `Int32GetDatum()` ([postgres.h#DatumGetInt32](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/postgres.h#L198-L216)). Whether a type is passed by value is recorded in `pg_type.typbyval`. Variable-length types are always passed by reference ([pg_type.h#typbyval](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/pg_type.h#L58-L66)). Function calls and executor slots pass values as a `Datum` plus a separate null flag ([fmgr.h:95](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/fmgr.h#L95), [tuptable.h:125-127](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/executor/tuptable.h#L125-L127)). `NullableDatum` bundles the two ([postgres.h#NullableDatum](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/postgres.h#L66-L79)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds, except that the conversions are macros rather than inline functions; `Datum` is still `uintptr_t` ([postgres.h#Datum](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/postgres.h#L357-L367), [postgres.h#DatumGetInt32](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/postgres.h#L472-L479)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds, except that, as in 12, the conversions are macros ([postgres.h#Datum](../raw/postgres-14/src/include/postgres.h#L401-L411), [postgres.h#DatumGetInt32](../raw/postgres-14/src/include/postgres.h#L516-L523)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds ([postgres.h#Datum](../raw/postgres-18/src/include/postgres.h#L59-L69)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Differs: `Datum` is always 8 bytes (`uint64_t`), even on 32-bit platforms, so it is no longer tied to pointer width ([postgres.h#Datum](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/postgres.h#L58-L76)). Built-in 8-byte types such as `float8`, `int8` and `timestamp` are therefore always passed by value ([pg_config_manual.h#USE_FLOAT8_BYVAL](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/pg_config_manual.h#L86-L92)).

Related: [fmgr](#fmgr), [Tuple](#tuple), [varlena](#varlena), [TOAST](#toast)

### Dead tuple

**Aliases:** dead row, dead row version, `n_dead_tup`, `HEAPTUPLE_DEAD`, `HEAPTUPLE_RECENTLY_DEAD`. **Checked on:** PostgreSQL 12, 14, 17, 18, 19.

A dead tuple is a row version that no longer belongs to the table's current contents: one replaced by a committed `UPDATE` or `DELETE`, or one written by an aborted transaction ([pgstat_relation.c:568-580](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat_relation.c#L568-L580)). It keeps using space until [pruning](#pruning) or [VACUUM](#vacuum) removes it. VACUUM uses `HeapTupleSatisfiesVacuum()` to sort row versions. `HEAPTUPLE_DEAD` means the version is dead and removable. `HEAPTUPLE_RECENTLY_DEAD` means it is dead but some transaction may still see it, so it must stay for now ([heapam.h#HTSV_Result](../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/heapam.h#L122-L130)). VACUUM turns removed versions into `LP_DEAD` [line pointers](#line-pointer) and collects their [TIDs](#tid) in `dead_items`, so that index entries can be removed before the pointers are freed ([vacuumlazy.c#LVRelState](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/heap/vacuumlazy.c#L176-L185)). The `n_dead_tup` column of `pg_stat_all_tables` is an estimate. Each committed update or delete adds one, and so does each row inserted or updated by an aborted transaction; VACUUM then overwrites the count with what it found ([system_views.sql:688](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/system_views.sql#L688), [pgstat_relation.c#AtEOXact_PgStat_Relations](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat_relation.c#L556-L580), [pgstat_relation.c#pgstat_report_vacuum](../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat_relation.c#L233-L234)).

**Version notes:**
- PostgreSQL 12: Holds. The visibility results and the `n_dead_tup` column are the same, and the statistics collector applies the same commit and abort rules and takes the count VACUUM reports ([heapam.h#HTSV_Result](../raw/postgres-12/src/include/access/heapam.h#L85-L93), [system_views.sql:567](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/catalog/system_views.sql#L567), [pgstat.c:2150-2152](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L2150-L2152), [pgstat.c:2160-2162](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L2160-L2162), [pgstat.c:6218-6219](../raw/postgres-12/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L6218-L6219)).
- PostgreSQL 14: Holds, as in 12 ([heapam.h#HTSV_Result](../raw/postgres-14/src/include/access/heapam.h#L92-L100), [system_views.sql:646](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/catalog/system_views.sql#L646), [pgstat.c:2422-2424](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L2422-L2424), [pgstat.c:2432-2434](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L2432-L2434), [pgstat.c:5209-5210](../raw/postgres-14/src/backend/postmaster/pgstat.c#L5209-L5210)).
- PostgreSQL 18: Holds ([heapam.h#HTSV_Result](../raw/postgres-18/src/include/access/heapam.h#L121-L129), [system_views.sql:697](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/catalog/system_views.sql#L697), [pgstat_relation.c:582-584](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat_relation.c#L582-L584), [pgstat_relation.c:592-594](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat_relation.c#L592-L594), [pgstat_relation.c:235-236](../raw/postgres-18/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat_relation.c#L235-L236)).
- PostgreSQL 19: Holds ([heapam.h#HTSV_Result](../raw/postgres-19/src/include/access/heapam.h#L135-L143), [system_views.sql:735](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/catalog/system_views.sql#L735), [pgstat_relation.c:583-585](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat_relation.c#L583-L585), [pgstat_relation.c:593-595](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat_relation.c#L593-L595), [pgstat_relation.c:235-236](../raw/postgres-19/src/backend/utils/activity/pgstat_relation.c#L235-L236)).
